interpretation.summary: A Pearson correlation was computed between x and y for the specified calendar-year window, using complete cases only. The analysis included 10 observations. The estimated Pearson correlation was 0.97549, with a ninety-five percent confidence interval from 0.89645 to 0.99438, and a p-value of 1.5341e-06. Because the p-value is below the five percent threshold, the result is classified as evidence of a positive linear association between x and y. This means that higher values of x tend to co-occur with higher values of y in this sample. The confidence interval indicates the range of plausible values for the correlation under the stated assumptions. The analysis is observational, so the association should not be interpreted as a causal relationship. The reported warnings note that Pearson correlation measures linear association only, and that design, linearity, and default inference assumptions are not guaranteed by these diagnostics.
limitations: This analysis does not establish causality.
Pearson correlation captures linear association only; non-linear relationships would not be detected.
The inference assumes independent observations, approximate normality, and no influential outliers, which were not verified here.
The confidence interval and p-value depend on the stated assumptions and may be sensitive to violations.
The analysis used complete cases only, so results may differ if missing data are not missing completely at random.
The study design is observational, so confounding and selection effects cannot be ruled out.
